newsitem.title: USA: Tyco Toys debt soars on Mattel merger news.
newsitem.headline: Tyco Toys debt soars on Mattel merger news.

text.p: Tyco Toys Inc's debt soared nearly four points on Monday fueled by news of its proposed merger with top toymaker Mattel Inc, corporate bond traders said.
"Tyco's debt traded up about four points on the board on about five million bonds," said one high-yield trader.

"After the news that Tyco was being taken over the debt took off...it was Merry Christmas for everybody especially if you owned the bonds." Tyco Toys' debt was quoted 105-3/8 bid, 105-1/2 offer in late afternoon trading, up four points from Friday's close at 101-1/2, traders said.
Traders said, however, no movement was seen in Mattel's debt by secondary market traders. Mattel debt consist primarily of medium-term notes, they said.
After the merger announcement, Moody's Investors Service affirmed Mattel's A3 medium-term notes and placed Tyco Toys' B3 senior subordinated debt under review for possible upgrade.
Moody's noted Mattel's strong market position as the largest global toy manufacturer, its increasing product diversity and its strong financial performance.
Also noting that, with the current debt on Tyco's balance sheet, the transaction could result in a modest increase in Mattel's consolidated debt levels.

The rating agency added that the further addition to Mattel's portfolio of toy brands should help to stengthen the company's position in negotitations with its largest customers that account for a very substantial proportion of its sales.
Tyco Toys radio-controlled segment of boy's toys, matchbox cars and Sesame Street line of licensed toys will join Mattel's already strong brands such as Barbie, Hotwheels, Disney and Fisher Price.
Meanwhile, Tyco's stock benifitted as well soaring 4-1/2 points to end the trading day at 11-1/2, while Mattel's stock fell 3/4 to 29-7/8.
Under the proposed merger agreement, Tyco shareholders will receive Mattel stock worth $12.50 for each Tyco share.

Earlier this year Mattel pursued Hasbro Inc for similar reasons, but was forced to drop its unsolicited offer due to concerns about antitrust implications associated with joning the nation's top two toymakers.
